newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex says retains majority of Queretero market.
newsitem.headline: Telmex says retains majority of Queretero market.

text.p: Former telephone monopoly Telefonos de Mexico said Friday it likely has maintained between 80 percent and 90 percent of the long-distance telephone market in the central city of Queretaro, company spokesman said.

Queretero, north of Mexico City, was the first city opened to competition with the New Year as Telmex, a former state-owned company that was privatized in 1990, finally lost its monopoly status after half a century.
"We are making all possible efforts to keep all clients, with estimates between 80 and 90 percent," Telmex spokesman Fernando Perez Valdez told Reuters.

However, a press release late Thursday from Alestra, the new competitor formed by Grupo Industrial Alfa, Bancomer and AT&T Corp, said it was chosen by 42 percent of long-distance subscribers in Queretero as of Dec. 28.
Official figures from the government's Federal Telecommunications Commission of Queretaro's long-distance market share have not been released yet.
The commission distributed 80,000 ballots for Queretaro residents to choose among seven long-distance carriers.
Competition will begin one-by-one in other large cities throughout the year.
